_README: Hand-placed meshes in EDITOR coordinates. EMPTY ON PURPOSE — the island's
fog is done with the game's own ExponentialHeightFog now (MTMI_FOG_PROPS,
or height_fog.json exported from the editor), not with meshes.
The mechanism still works and is kept for placing one-off props without
an editor round-trip. Fields: name (prefix _ to disable), X/Y/Z, scale,
Yaw, mesh. Add "world": true for world-space coordinates.
WHY NO MESH FOG — three attempts, all invisible in game, recorded so none
of them gets tried again:
1. Volume-domain material (the original SM_Fog meshes). Must be voxelized
into the volumetric fog grid; that never happened however correct the
asset was. Motor Town has never voxelized a Volume material into fog:
of 22,125 cooked assets exactly one carries voxelization shaders, and
it is the engine's stock cloud material. See TODO section 4.
2. SM_Particle_Smoke_01a / Mat_Gradient_01. Surface + additive, so no
voxelization needed, still invisible at 30x, 100x and 300x. Its cooked
shader map carries FMeshParticleVertexFactory: an FX material wanting
per-particle input a static mesh cannot supply.
3. SM_Generic_Cloud_* / Mat_Cloud. Also invisible, and this one was never
explained. Mesh and material both ship in the base pak at the paths
used, the mesh imports the material correctly, and Mat_Cloud cooks
Local + InstancedStaticMesh + SplineMesh with no particle dependency —
the same profile as meshes that do render.
None of it was placement. Seven water tanks at the seven coordinates the
fog had occupied were ALL visible, including one 9 m above the delivery
actor, which is what finally ruled the coordinates out and pointed at the
height fog instead.
